# FOR005 `cpu-time-for-wall-clock`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="enabled by default" />

`cpu_time` measures time in code that runs in parallel (OpenMP, OpenACC, MPI).

## Why

`cpu_time` returns processor time of the calling process or thread, not elapsed time. With
threads it adds up (or not, depending on the compiler) the time of all threads; with a GPU it
reports almost nothing, because the host thread just waits. Measure elapsed time with
`system_clock` (count and count_rate), `omp_get_wtime()` or `MPI_Wtime()`, after synchronising
asynchronous work (`!$acc wait`).

## Reported

```fortran
call cpu_time(t0)
```

## Preferred

```fortran
call system_clock(c0, rate)
...
call system_clock(c1)
elapsed = real(c1 - c0) / rate
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[FOR005] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = FOR005` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/fobos/lint).
